title: Persisted opt-out for the per-repo quest skill (skill_source=plugin equivalent), mirroring lore's LCLI-443/444
description:
Directed by opum-agent (OPAG-41 cross-session ruling, 2026-09-05): the second, opt-out half of retiring per-repo Claude Code skill distribution, mirroring lore-cli's LCLI-443/444 exactly. Depends on QCLI-235 (the opum-quest plugin scaffold) for the nudge text to have somewhere to point and for dogfooding.

lore-cli's shipped shape (LCLI-443, corrected by LCLI-444 - read both task records in full before implementing):

- Config: `[agents] skill_source = "plugin"` in .lore/config.toml (SKILL_SOURCES = ["repo","plugin"], default "repo" = today's behavior unchanged). Resolution: file value overlaid on default, invalid value fails with a named validation diagnostic.
- CLI flag: `lore init --skill-source <repo|plugin>` persists it via a byte-preserving regex splice into the existing TOML (not a full reserialize) - preserves every unrelated comment/byte in the file. There is no per-invocation override flag on `lore agents` itself; only `lore init --skill-source` writes the persisted value.
- "Explicit beats config": `applyAgentsBridge`'s `skillSource` is read from config ONLY for the bare `lore agents` command (`includeCodex: true`); a scoped explicit request (`lore init --claude`/`--agents`) hardcodes `skillSource: "repo"` regardless of the persisted value, so an explicit ask always still materializes the file.
- Orphan-drift model (`planSkill`, straight `===` string equality against the deterministic generated template, BOM/CRLF-normalized before comparing): under `skill_source: "plugin"`, a present skill file is ALWAYS reported `orphaned` (drift, exit 6 under --check) UNLESS `--force` is given on a non-check run AND the file is byte-identical to the generated output, in which case it's `removed` instead. A file that differs (hand-edited, or generated by an older CLI version) is NEVER removed, even under --force - it stays `orphaned` permanently until deleted by hand or restored to exact generated bytes.
- CLAUDE.md nudge line varies by skill_source (this is exactly the bug LCLI-444 found and fixed - `buildNudgeBody` originally ignored `skillSource` entirely): `"- **Skill:** installed from the \`opum-lore\` Claude Code plugin, not this repository - how to drive lore."` vs the unchanged `"- **Skill:** \`.claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md\` - how to drive lore."`
- No new exit code or JSON envelope shape - `orphaned`/`removed` reuse the existing drift/exit-6 machinery, just two new literal values in what was a closed action union (a breaking addition any exhaustive downstream switch must handle).
- LCLI-444 also dogfooded: lore-cli's own .lore/config.toml now has `skill_source = "plugin"` and its own .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md is deleted.

quest-cli's starting point is NOT identical to lore's - read this carefully before implementing, do not just port lore's TOML text verbatim:

- Config storage: quest-cli's workspace config is .quest/workspace.toml with a FLAT three-field schema (schemaVersion, name, taskIdPrefix - WorkspaceConfiguration type, src/ports/workspaces.ts:30-34) and NO nested-table concept at all today, unlike lore's .lore/config.toml which already had per-table Zod-loose-object tolerance to extend. This task must DECIDE and BUILD the config storage shape (a new field on workspace.toml, and the schema/serialize/adapter-read machinery to support it), not assume table nesting already exists.
- Skill-file protection: quest-cli's `updateQuestSkillFile` (agent-instructions.ts:161-170) unconditionally overwrites the skill file on ANY drift or absence today - there is no `protected`/hand-edit-guard concept and no `--force` flag on `quest agents` at all currently. This task adds BOTH the opt-out AND the first-ever hand-edit protection for this file (lore already had `protected` semantics to extend; quest-cli does not).
- Target-path interaction: quest's skill file path (questSkillPath) does NOT vary by --target today (unlike the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instructions block, which does via agentInstructionPathForTarget, QCLI-227). Decide and record explicitly whether the opt-out applies only under --target claude (since a Claude Code marketplace plugin is a Claude-Code-specific concept) or unconditionally regardless of target.
- No CHANGELOG.md exists in quest-cli (confirmed) - use docs/reference/quest-cli-release-truth.md's per-release section convention plus this task's own final summary as the durable record, matching every other quest-cli change this session. lore's own precedent: LCLI-444 (the dogfooding/bugfix follow-up) added no separate CHANGELOG bullet of its own, only LCLI-443 (the originating feature) did - if this task similarly splits into a feature part and a same-cycle bugfix/dogfooding part, only the feature part needs the doc-note.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A design decision is recorded AND implemented for where this config value lives (extending .quest/workspace.toml's schema) and what it's called, including the schema/serialize/adapter-read machinery actually built - not assumed to already support nested tables the way lore's .lore/config.toml did

Under the opt-in setting, quest agents --check/--update-instructions neither writes nor proposes .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md; a leftover file is reported as drift (exit 6 under --check) naming the file and the remedy; default/unset behavior is verified unchanged byte-for-byte against the existing test suite

A new --force flag on quest agents removes a leftover skill file only when it is byte-identical to quest's own generated questSkillContent; a hand-edited or otherwise-differing file is left in place even under --force - note in the implementation that this is also the first time quest-cli's skill file gains any hand-edit protection at all, since today it has none

An explicit, scoped write request (quest init --agent-instructions, or an equivalent explicit flag) always still materializes the skill file regardless of the persisted opt-out setting - 'explicit beats config', tested directly
A decision is recorded and implemented for whether the opt-out applies only under --target claude or unconditionally, given questSkillPath does not vary by --target today

The CLAUDE.md managed-instructions-block prose (or an equivalent nudge) reflects the opt-out, telling a reader the quest skill comes from the opum-quest plugin rather than this repository, mirroring lore's LCLI-444 fix for the identical bug class (a nudge whose text didn't vary by the new setting)
Tests cover: default unchanged, opt-in (no write/propose + drift report + force-removal-only-on-byte-match + hand-edit-never-removed), and explicit-request-overrides-opt-in

This repository (quest-cli itself) is dogfooded once QCLI-235's plugin scaffold exists: quest-cli's own workspace config is set to the opt-in value and its own .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md is deleted, mirroring LCLI-444

implementationNotes: AC1: added an optional agentSkillSource field (WorkspaceConfiguration, src/ports/workspaces.ts) stored as a TOML [agents] table (skill_source key) rather than a top-level flat key, matching the ruling's 'agents-style table' framing. Built the table-scoped parser (tomlTableString, src/adapters/workspaces/local-workspaces.ts) since the existing tomlString helper matches a key ANYWHERE in the file with no table awareness at all - confirmed this would have let a same-named key outside [agents] false-match, and added a test proving it doesn't. serializeConfiguration only emits the [agents] block when set, so every pre-existing workspace.toml is untouched. NOT a schemaVersion bump. Proved backward compatibility empirically rather than assuming it: installed the published @opum-ai/quest 0.3.3 in an isolated temp dir, hand-wrote a workspace.toml carrying the new [agents] table (exactly the format the new code emits), and ran 0.3.3's own doctor/task create/task list/agents --check against it - all four exited 0 with no error, confirming 0.3.3's flat-regex parser silently ignores the unrecognized table rather than choking on it.

AC2/AC3: checkQuestSkillFile/updateQuestSkillFile/inspectQuestSkillFile (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts) now take a skillSource param. Under plugin: absent file -> state current (healthy, not 'missing'); present file -> state orphaned (new AgentInstructionCheck union member) regardless of content, exit 6 under --check, naming the file and the remedy. A new --force flag on quest agents (src/cli/main.ts) removes it ONLY when force && current === questSkillContent (byte-exact) - this doubles as the skill file's first-ever hand-edit guard, since updateQuestSkillFile previously had zero protection at all (unconditional overwrite). Added AgentInstructionPort.remove() (new port method) and its LocalAgentInstructionPort implementation, with the same symlink/absolute-path guards as read/write.

AC4: quest init --agent-instructions always calls updateQuestSkillFile with skillSource defaulted to 'repo' (unaffected by any --skill-source passed in the same call or already persisted) - explicit beats config, mirroring lore's includeCodex-scoped hardcode exactly. Only the bare 'quest agents' command (via new resolveAgentSkillSource helper) reads the persisted config value. Tested directly: init --agent-instructions --skill-source plugin writes the skill file once in that same call, then a later bare agents --update-instructions reports the now-existing file as orphaned instead of leaving it alone.

AC5: ruled unconditional - the skill file's existence is a distribution question, not a --target question (the instructions BLOCK varies by target because it's about which file carries the block; the skill file's path never varied by target even before this task). Implemented exactly that: no --target parameter threaded into the skill-file functions at all.

AC6: fixed a latent staleness bug found while implementing this - questSkillContent's 'quest instructions' bullet hardcoded 'managed in AGENTS.md', now reads 'managed in this project's agent-instructions file (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, depending on how this repository configured quest agents --update-instructions)', since QCLI-227 made AGENTS.md no longer the only possible target. This is the quest-side nudge; there was no separate opum-quest-plugin-vs-repo distinction to add here since (per AC5) skill-file distribution doesn't depend on which instructions file this repo uses.

AC7: 10 new tests added. Unit-level (test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts): absent-is-current, present-is-orphaned, non-force leaves it, force removes only byte-exact, force never removes hand-edited. Unit-level (test/integration/workspaces/local-workspaces.test.ts): agentSkillSource round-trips as [agents] table, a same-named key outside the table never matches, invalid value throws invalid_configuration, reconfigure changes it independently of name/taskIdPrefix. CLI end-to-end (test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts): full init-to-force-removal flow including the exact workspace.toml bytes written, --force never deleting a hand-edited file end-to-end, invalid --skill-source usage error, --reconfigure accepting --skill-source alone, and agents --check in an uninitialized directory still defaulting to repo (proving resolveAgentSkillSource's not_initialized fallback works, since agents --check has never required init). Full bun run check: 413/413 tests (403 prior + 10 new), typecheck/lint(2 pre-existing unrelated warnings)/format/layer all clean.

AC8 (dogfooding): quest-cli's own .quest/workspace.toml now carries [agents]\nskill_source = "plugin"; its own .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md is deleted (confirmed byte-exact match required before removal succeeded - first brought it to 'current' via a plain --update-instructions, since it had independently drifted this session from the AC6 text fix, then --target claude --force removed it cleanly). Caught and self-corrected one operator mistake during dogfooding: an initial --force run omitted --target claude and regenerated AGENTS.md via the unrelated, independent --target default (codex) - not a bug in this task's code, just a reminder that --target and --skill-source are orthogonal flags governing different files. Removed the accidental AGENTS.md and redid it correctly; recorded here rather than silently fixed so the distinction is on record.
finalSummary: Mirrored lore-cli's LCLI-443/444 skill_source opt-out for quest's own per-repo Claude Code skill, adapted to quest-cli's simpler starting point: a new optional [agents] table in .quest/workspace.toml (agentSkillSource, additive, no schemaVersion bump - empirically proved the published 0.3.3 tolerates it via a real install), a first-ever hand-edit guard on the skill file (previously unconditionally overwritten), a new --force flag that only ever removes a byte-exact leftover, unconditional (not --target-scoped) opt-out per the ruling that skill distribution and instructions-block targeting are orthogonal concerns, and 'explicit beats config' via quest init --agent-instructions always materializing the file regardless of the persisted setting. Dogfooded on quest-cli itself: workspace.toml now declares skill_source=plugin and .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md is deleted. 10 new tests (unit + CLI end-to-end), full bun run check green (413/413), lore check and quest doctor both clean.
